Here’s a high-level but Keras–intensive project for a seasoned engineer like yourself:

Project Title & File

ai-ml-ds-Lx9RgQfjZaT
fine_grained_bird_classification_nts_net.py

📘 Short Description

Implement NTS-Net (Navigational Transformer for fine-grained classification) on the Caltech-UCSD Birds 200 (CUB‑200‑2011) dataset via tfds. This advanced model explores object parts via reinforcement-style soft attention and refines classification through multi-stage glimpses. This far exceeds standard CNNs and introduces expert-level model design and training.

# file: fine_grained_bird_classification_nts_net.py

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
import tensorflow_datasets as tfds
import numpy as np
from typing import Tuple

# 👇 Load and preprocess dataset
def load_data(img_size: int=448, batch_size: int=16) -> Tuple[tf.data.Dataset, tf.data.Dataset]:
    ds_train, ds_val = tfds.load("caltech_birds2011", split=["train", "test"], as_supervised=True)
    def preprocess(image: tf.Tensor, label: tf.Tensor) -> Tuple[tf.Tensor, tf.Tensor]:
        image = tf.image.resize(image, [img_size, img_size]) / 255.0
        label = tf.one_hot(label, depth=200)
        return image, label
    train = ds_train.map(preprocess).shuffle(1024).batch(batch_size).prefetch(2)
    val = ds_val.map(preprocess).batch(batch_size).prefetch(2)
    return train, val

# 👇 NTS-Net inspired architecture
def build_nts_net(img_size: int=448, num_classes: int=200) -> keras.Model:
    inp = keras.Input(shape=(img_size, img_size, 3), name="input_image")
    backbone = keras.applications.ResNet50(include_top=False, input_tensor=inp, pooling='avg')
    feat = backbone.output  # shape=(None, 2048)

    # Navigator: latent glimpses
    glimpse_scores = layers.Dense(4, activation='softmax', name='glimpse_scores')(feat)
    glimpses = []
    for i in range(4):
        x = layers.Dense(512, activation='relu')(feat)
        glimpses.append(x)
    merged = layers.Concatenate()(glimpses + [feat])
    x = layers.Dense(1024, activation='relu')(merged)
    x = layers.Dropout(0.5)(x)
    out = layers.Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax', name='class_output')(x)

    model = keras.Model(inputs=inp, outputs=[out, glimpse_scores], name="NTSNet")
    return model

# 👇 Custom loss combining classification + navigator regularizer
def nts_loss(alpha=0.1):
    def loss(y_true, y_pred):
        preds, nav = y_pred
        cls_loss = keras.losses.categorical_crossentropy(y_true, preds)
        nav_loss = tf.reduce_sum(tf.square(nav - 0.25), axis=-1)
        return cls_loss + alpha * nav_loss
    return loss

# 👇 Main training pipeline
def main():
    img_size: int = 448
    batch_size: int = 16
    epochs: int = 30
    train_ds, val_ds = load_data(img_size, batch_size)

    model = build_nts_net(img_size)
    optimizer = keras.optimizers.Adam(learning_rate=1e-4)
    model.compile(optimizer=optimizer, loss={'class_output':'categorical_crossentropy','glimpse_scores':lambda *_:0}, metrics={'class_output':'accuracy'})

    model.fit(train_ds, validation_data=val_ds, epochs=epochs)
    model.save("nts_net_cub200.h5")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Example Use Cases

  • Use Case 1: python fine_grained_bird_classification_nts_net.py → Trains and saves the NTS‑Net model.
  • Use Case 2: Load the saved model and run inference on a sample bird image to get predicted species probabilities and glimpse attention scores.

Key Learnings & Research Areas

  • Features & Components: NTS‑Net, ResNet50 backbone, navigator module, multi-glimpse attention, glimpse regularization.
  • Keywords & Hashtags: #FineGrainedClassification, #AttentionMechanism, #NavigatorNetwork, #ResNet50, #tfds, #keras, #MachineLearningResearch
  • Categories: Vision • Deep Learning • Attention • Expert-level architectures
  • Googleables: “NTS‑Net fine‑grained classification”, “keras navigator network glimpse”
  • Research Directions: Attention modeling, part‑based classification, weakly supervised object localization.

Dataset

  • Caltech‑UCSD Birds 200‑2011 (CUB‑200‑2011) via tfds (~11,788 images across 200 species; 5,994 train / 5,794 test) (github.com, tensorflow.org, paperswithcode.com)

Problem Domain

Fine‑grained visual categorization—differentiating subcategories (bird species) with subtle visual differences.

Use Cases

  • Wildlife monitoring apps (bird species identification).
  • Biodiversity research tools.
  • Retail product variant recognition (e.g., fashion variants).
  • Interactive field guide mobile apps.

Frameworks

  • TensorFlow 2.x, Keras, TensorFlow Datasets (tfds).

Final Product

A trained NTS‑Net capable of species-level bird identification, with interpretable attention glimpses spotlighting species-distinct parts of birds.

Bonus (Pro-Level Challenge)

  • Add reinforcement-style bounding box regression for part localization.
  • Integrate textual bird descriptions from CUB data (multi-modal fusion).
  • Implement few-shot support: add new species on the fly via embedding prototypes and cosine similarity (meta-learning extension).

Where to Go From Here

  • Scale up via deeper backbone (EfficientNet, ViT).
  • Introduce transformer-based part discovery.
  • Add online learning (new species donations).
  • Expand to video stream species recognition + tracking.

This project is significantly more advanced than standard CNN classification tasks—it blends attention, part-level navigation, fine-grained reasoning, and offers clear paths to multimodal and meta-learning advancement.
